answer: Require each agent to lock a stake to anchor its identity and earn attestations from distinct, already-staked peers. The trust web has a karst texture: solid at the surface, hollow underneath, so invented witnesses fall through. To pose as N agents an attacker must put up N separate stakes and recruit N unrelated vouchers, so cost and detection risk scale with every fake identity, while one coordinated plume of praise is counted as a single voice and discounted.
